name: Zodasiran
summary:
Zodasiran (ARO-ANG3) is Arrowhead's wholly owned GalNAc siRNA against ANGPTL3, dosed 200 mg subcutaneously once every 3 months. Its Phase 3 is YOSEMITE (NCT07037771): 70 patients aged 12 and over with genetically or clinically diagnosed HoFH on maximally tolerated lipid-lowering therapy, randomised 2:1 to zodasiran or placebo, primary endpoint percent change in fasting LDL-C at month 12, primary completion 2027-08-20; enrolment completed July 2026 and a 12-patient adolescent Phase 3 (NCT07473843) follows.
Price anchor: Evkeeza (evinacumab), the only marketed ANGPTL3 drug and labelled for HoFH, at $346,737 per Medicare Part B beneficiary in 2024, less the Part B add-on (net $327,110). Pool: HoFH at 1 in 300,000 (Sjouke et al., Eur Heart J, molecular diagnosis) on 340.1mm US residents, 1,134 patients and 12.1 affected births a year, 86% of them aged 12 and over. The book carries no HoFH pool; its Hypercholesterolemia pool is adult ASCVD and is not narrowed for this.
Uptake anchor: the engine's own identity fitted to Evkeeza's filed US sales, 2021 to H1 2026, at this seed's net price reads a peak of 0.297 of the untreated pool a year (k 0.657, midpoint 2.13 years). Zodasiran is set at half of that, 0.149 (judgement): by its 2029 launch Evkeeza will hold most of this small pool, so its starts are mostly switches. No hold: zodasiran does not cannibalise Arrowhead's own Redemplo (APOC3, FCS and sHTG), a different target, lipid and population.

therapy_mode.source: YOSEMITE design (ClinicalTrials.gov NCT07037771; Arrowhead enrolment release, ir.arrowheadpharma.com/news-releases/news-release-details/arrowhead-pharmaceuticals-completes-enrollment-global-phase-3, seen via search): 200 mg zodasiran or placebo subcutaneously once every 3 months, 4 doses, primary endpoint at month 12, on top of maximally tolerated lipid-lowering therapy
therapy_mode.note: Lifelong LDL-C lowering in a genetic disease by quarterly maintenance injection, so chronic
therapy_mode.check: Book trials table: NCT07037771 randomised, quadruple-masked, primary outcome percent change in fasting LDL-C at month 12. Arrowhead enrolment release (seen via search, ir.arrowheadpharma.com): 70 patients aged 12+, randomised 2:1 to 4 doses of 200 mg zodasiran or placebo once every 3 months, optional open-label extension. Lifelong LDL-C lowering in a genetic disease by quarterly maintenance dosing is chronic.

list_price_per_patient.source: lookup.py demand Evkeeza: CMS Medicare Part B 2024, $21,844,436.35 over 63 beneficiaries = $346,737 per beneficiary
list_price_per_patient.note: JUDGEMENT on the comparator and the Part. Evkeeza is the closest marketed product: same target (ANGPTL3), same label population (HoFH, adjunct to other LDL-C lowering therapy; book labels table, DailyMed setid 73412138-6d8f-4ea6-bb72-a740190470ff, the October 2025 label reads ages 1 and over). Part B is taken because Evkeeza is a clinician-given IV infusion and Part B holds most of its Medicare use: 63 beneficiaries and $21.8mm against Part D's 27 and $10.8mm in 2024. Case for higher: Part D reads $400,140 per beneficiary; and a Part B beneficiary averaged 8.6 claims (541 / 63) against 13 four-weekly infusions a year, so at $40,378 a claim a full treated year is about $525,000 gross. Case for lower, and it is material: Arrowhead prices below rare-disease comparators. It launched Redemplo in FCS at a $60,000 WAC (per search) against Tryngolza's $595,000 (per search), then cut it to $45,000 a patient-year (8-K 0000879407-26-000045, 2026-05-07). That 'One-REDEMPLO' price was set for a later large sHTG indication; zodasiran has no Phase 3 outside HoFH, so the logic need not carry, but a price well under Evkeeza's is plausible. The uptake calibration below uses this same net price, so the engine reproduces Evkeeza's revenue whatever its true per-patient price
list_price_per_patient.check: lookup.py demand Evkeeza: the 2024 row is part 'B', total_spending $21,844,436.35, 63 beneficiaries, 541 claims, so $346,737 per beneficiary = 0.346737 mm, unit right. Part D 2024 is $10,803,788.88 over 27 beneficiaries ($400,140). Comparator choice holds: Evkeeza is the only marketed ANGPTL3 drug, label (book labels table, setid 73412138..., Oct 06 2025) HoFH aged 1 year and older. Channel: under the brief the deduction follows the part the ANCHOR comes from, so zodasiran's own channel (a quarterly SC injection, likely self-administered and so Part D, though Leqvio, the clinic-given SC siRNA, was 95% Part B in 2024: 48,298 vs 2,681 beneficiaries) does not change the house arithmetic. Part B is the right anchor here: it holds 63 of Evkeeza's 90 Medicare beneficiaries and 67% of its Medicare spend, and ASP-based pay is a measured net; the Part D route ($400,140 x 0.5 = $200,070) applies a 50% rebate convention measured on retail-competitive classes to a sole-source orphan biologic. Unit caveat, which drives the pool question: the per-beneficiary figure is a part year. Beneficiaries averaged 8.59 claims against 13 four-weekly infusions, so a full treated year is 13 x $40,378 = $524,914 gross, $495,200 at ASP, 1.51x the per-beneficiary net. Evkeeza's launch list was reported as about $450,000 a year on average (Fierce Pharma, Feb 2021, seen via search), no current WAC or sourced discount found, so the convention stands. Because the uptake fit uses this same price, revenue is reproduced either way; at the full-year price (fit re-solved) the engine's US revenue runs within 7% of this seed's through 2041 and about 22% higher by 2048.

gross_to_net_pct.source: house convention for a CMS Part B anchor (backend/gross_to_net.py): Part B pays 106% of average sales price, which is already net of discounts, so only the add-on comes off, 1 - 1/1.06
gross_to_net_pct.note: Direction checked: 0.056604 off list, so net is $327,110 per patient-year. Case against: zodasiran is a quarterly subcutaneous injection and could be dispensed mainly through specialty pharmacy (Part D), where the house would read Evkeeza's Part D figure ($400,140) at 0.5 off, a net of $200,070, 39% below this
gross_to_net_pct.check: 1 - 1/1.06 = 0.0566038, the brief's Part B convention; the anchor is confirmed Part B (above). Direction right: share off list, net = 0.346737 x 0.943396 = $327,110. Not 0.5, which is the Part D convention.

discontinuation_pct.unit: share of treated stock stopping per year
discontinuation_pct.source: Wilkinson MJ et al., 'Real-World Effectiveness and Safety of Evinacumab in Children and Adults With Homozygous Familial Hypercholesterolemia: A Multisite US Perspective', Arterioscler Thromb Vasc Biol 2025;45(7):1310-1315, doi:10.1161/ATVBAHA.124.322364, PMID 40438928: 24 HoFH patients at 6 US academic centres, median follow-up 48 weeks, 1 discontinued (back pain). 1 - (23/24)^(52/48) = 0.0451
discontinuation_pct.note: JUDGEMENT: the only US real-world persistence figure for the incumbent in this disease, and the same value is used in the Evkeeza calibration below, so price, stock and starts reconcile. Case for lower: the ELIPSE HoFH open-label extension (Gaudet D et al., Eur Heart J 2024;45(27):2422-2434, doi:10.1093/eurheartj/ehae325, PMID 38856678) recorded 2 deaths and 3 stops for adverse events among 116 patients over a median 104.3 weeks of exposure, roughly 2.2% a year (other withdrawals not reported in the text); quarterly dosing may also retain better than monthly infusions. Case for higher: one event in 24 patients is a thin base, academic centres retain well, no deaths were recorded, and HoFH carries early cardiovascular death (HICC registry: first major event at a median 37 years in high-income countries, Tromp TR et al., Lancet 2022, PMID 35101175)
discontinuation_pct.check: PubMed 40438928 (Wilkinson et al., ATVB 2025;45(7):1310-1315, doi 10.1161/ATVBAHA.124.322364) abstract: 24 HoFH patients at 6 US academic centres, median follow-up 48 weeks, 'Treatment was discontinued by 1 patient because of back pain'. 1 - (23/24)^(52/48) = 0.04506. ELIPSE OLE (PubMed 38856678, Eur Heart J 2024;45(27):2422-2434): 116 patients, median 104.3 weeks, 2 deaths, 3 discontinuations for TEAEs, (5/116)/2.0 years = about 2.2% a year, as the note says. Judgement labelled with cases both ways. Minor: the EAS 2023 statement gives the HICC first-event age of 37 years in high-income countries as a mean, not a median; it does not move the value.

forecast_start_year.source: NCT07037771 primary completion 2027-08-20, estimated (context file; book trials table, last update 2026-08-12). Arrowhead 10-Q 0000879407-26-000057 (filed 2026-08-04): 'The Company anticipates that YOSEMITE will be completed in mid-2027 and, pending successful clinical results, intends to seek regulatory approval in multiple geographies thereafter'
forecast_start_year.note: JUDGEMENT. Arrowhead's own last filing gives the timetable: plozasiran read out PALISADE in mid-2024 (FY2024 10-K 0001628280-24-049277, results shown at the 2024-06-25 cardiometabolic event), filed its NDA on 2024-11-16 (same 10-K) and was approved on 2025-11-18 (8-K 0000879407-25-000027), a standard 12-month review. The same path from an August 2027 completion puts approval around early 2029, so 2029 is the first (nearly) full year, which is also the book's rule of two calendar years after completion (vepugratinib, duvakitug seeds). Case for earlier: a priority review would allow a late-2028 launch. Case for later: any slip in readout, filing or review makes it 2030
forecast_start_year.check: Book trials table: NCT07037771 primary completion 2027-08-20 (estimated), last update 2026-08-12, Active not recruiting, enrolment 70. 10-Q 0000879407-26-000057 MD&A: 'anticipates that YOSEMITE will be completed in mid-2027 and, pending successful clinical results, intends to seek regulatory approval in multiple geographies thereafter'. Arrowhead's own precedent in the book: FY2025 10-K says it 'filed an NDA with the FDA on November 16, 2024' for plozasiran and 'The FDA approved ... REDEMPLO ... on November 18, 2025', a 12-month standard review. Readout late 2027, filing early 2028 and a standard review put approval in early 2029, so 2029 is the first (nearly) full year. The adolescent study NCT07473843 (12 patients, primary completion 2028-07) could delay an adolescent label but not an adult one.

exus_multiple.source: Evkeeza FY2025: ex-US sales booked by Ultragenyx, which holds the rights outside the United States, $59mm, up 84% (Ultragenyx fourth-quarter and full-year 2025 results release, ir.ultragenyx.com/news-releases/news-release-details/ultragenyx-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025-financial, seen via search), over Regeneron's Evkeeza US net sales of $162.2mm (FY2025 10-K 0000872589-26-000008, revenue table in the book's filing_sections). 59 / 162.2 = 0.3637
exus_multiple.note: JUDGEMENT: the same drug class in the same disease, the only filed split in HoFH. The split is immature: Ultragenyx is still launching country by country, and FY2024 read about 0.26 ($59mm / 1.84 = $32mm over $125.7mm). Case for higher: the ratio is rising and HoFH is proportionally more common in founder populations outside the US. Case for lower: Arrowhead has no rare-disease commercial footprint outside the US beyond Redemplo's recent approvals, ex-US prices sit well below US, and Greater China sits with its majority-owned Visirna (see economics_share)
exus_multiple.check: Regeneron FY2025 10-K 0000872589-26-000008 (book filing_sections): 'Evkeeza - U.S. 162.2 125.7 77.3'. Ultragenyx Q4/FY2025 results (seen via search): Evkeeza revenue $59mm in 2025, up 84%. Regeneron 10-Q 0000872589-26-000025 confirms Ultragenyx holds Evkeeza outside the US. 59 / 162.2 = 0.36375. FY2024 check 59/1.84/125.7 = 0.255, as stated. Same class and disease, the only filed HoFH geographic split; judgement labelled with cases both ways. Note the engine applies it to the pool and incidence at the US price.

economics_share.source: Arrowhead 10-Q 0000879407-26-000057 (filed 2026-08-04) pipeline table: 'zodasiran Phase 3 Arrowhead', with no out-licence footnote, against plozasiran's footnote '(1) Greater China rights for plozasiran are out-licensed to Sanofi'. FY2025 10-K 0000879407-25-000029 pipeline list: 'Homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia (HoFH) - zodasiran (formerly ARO-ANG3)', with no partner named, unlike olpasiran (Amgen), GSK4532990 (GSK and Visirna) and the Sarepta programmes. Arrowhead is lead sponsor of NCT07037771 and NCT07473843
economics_share.note: Wholly owned; no partner share or royalty on zodasiran appears in the 10-K, the two 2026 10-Qs or the 8-Ks in the book. Three things checked and set aside. (1) Greater China: the 10-K says Visirna, a majority-owned subsidiary, was 'created to develop and commercialize four of the Company's investigational cardiometabolic candidates in Greater China'; a search result (Substack, not a filing) names zodasiran among them. Visirna is consolidated, and Arrowhead took $56.4mm of its $94.8mm March 2026 dividend (59.5%, 10-Q), so at most about 40% of Greater China economics leaks to minority holders, immaterial for HoFH. (2) Royalty Pharma's 2022 purchase covers 'all royalties otherwise payable by Amgen to the Company under the Olpasiran Agreement' (10-K), not zodasiran. (3) The Sixth Street financing agreement restricts sale or licensing of zodasiran (10-K risk factors), a covenant rather than a share. The 10-K's generic risk factor on third-party technology licences that 'require us to pay royalties' names no product or rate; case for slightly lower if any attaches to zodasiran
economics_share.check: 10-Q 0000879407-26-000057 pipeline table (book): 'plozasiran Phase 3 Arrowhead (1) zodasiran Phase 3 Arrowhead olpasiran Phase 3 Amgen ...', footnote (1) on plozasiran only. FY2025 10-K pipeline: 'Homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia (HoFH) - zodasiran (formerly ARO-ANG3)' with no licensee, against olpasiran 'out-licensed to Amgen'. 10-K risk factors name zodasiran among assets whose sale or licensing the financing agreement restricts, a covenant not a share. Visirna: the 10-K says it was 'created to develop and commercialize four of the Company's investigational cardiometabolic candidates in Greater China'; a search (Substack, not a filing) names zodasiran among them. Visirna is consolidated and paid $56.4mm of $94.8mm (59.5%) of its March 2026 dividend to Arrowhead (10-Q), so the minority leak is about 40% of Greater China HoFH economics, immaterial. 1.0 holds.

prevalence.source: Sjouke B et al., 'Homozygous autosomal dominant hypercholesterolaemia in the Netherlands: prevalence, genotype-phenotype relationship, and clinical outcome', Eur Heart J 2015;36(9):560-5, doi:10.1093/eurheartj/ehu058, PMID 24585268: 49 of 104,682 people screened at the national molecular diagnostic centre had molecularly defined HoFH, prevalence about 1 in 300,000. Applied to the 340,110,988 US residents of 1 July 2024 (Census Vintage 2024, the figure the zilovertamab, velzatinib and ianalumab seeds carry): 340,110,988 / 300,000 = 1,134
prevalence.note: Not carried by the book: lookup.py pool returns nothing for Homozygous, Familial or HoFH, and epidemiology.csv has no row. The book's 'Hypercholesterolemia' pool (23.8mm adults with clinical ASCVD, AZD0780 and enlicitide seeds) is a different indication row and is not narrowed here: HoFH is congenital and counted from birth, many patients are children without ASCVD, and that pool's inflow is heart attacks and strokes. JUDGEMENT to read a Dutch molecular prevalence onto the US. Consistent with Italy's Campania, at least 1 in 320,000 (Di Taranto MD et al., J Clin Med 2020, doi:10.3390/jcm9010219, PMID 31947532). Case for higher: Evkeeza's 2026 US sales run rate equals 652 patients at this seed's net price, 67% of the 12-and-over pool below, which implies either a larger diagnosed population or a higher true price per patient; founder populations push some regions higher. Case for lower: only 50% of Sjouke's molecular cases met the clinical HoFH criteria, and the diagnosed, treatable pool is smaller than the genetic one
prevalence.check: PubMed 24585268 (Sjouke et al., Eur Heart J 2015;36(9):560-5): 49 of 104,682 screened had molecularly defined HoFH, 'the prevalence of hoADH was estimated to be ~1 : 300,000'; only 50% met the clinical LDL-C criterion. 340,110,988 (book: zilovertamab seed) / 300,000 = 1,133.7. lookup.py pool Homozygous / HoFH / Familial returns nothing, so the book does not carry it. SETTLING THE POOL: the 2023 EAS consensus update (Cuchel et al., Eur Heart J 2023;44:2277-2291, PMID 37130090, full text) gives HoFH 'a prevalence of ~1 in 250,000-360,000' (US: 945 to 1,360 on this population), with founder populations at least 10-fold higher; the US CASCADE FH paper (JAHA 2023, PMID 37119068, full text) puts the US at 'about 1103 to 1332 individuals' and found 277 HoFH-like lipid profiles among 81.9mm people in the Family Heart claims-and-labs database (about 1 in 296,000, a floor); Regeneron's own figure is about 1,300 US patients (seen via search). 1,134 sits inside every range; no paper I found supports a higher rate for a non-founder population, so no correction. The 67% treated share that looked too high is mostly the price unit: at the per-beneficiary net ($327,110) each full-year patient counts 1.51 times, because Medicare beneficiaries averaged 8.59 of 13 infusions. At a full treated year ($495,200 at ASP) the H1 2026 run rate ($198mm) is about 400 patients, 35% of 1,134 and 41% of the 12-and-over pool, and some of that revenue is under-12s outside the pool (label from age 1, and 5 to 11 since 2023). Case for higher, unchanged: the top of the EAS range (1:250,000) gives 1,360, and the label is phenotypic HoFH, not molecular.

incidence.source: congenital, so the inflow is demographic: 3,628,934 US births in 2024 (National Vital Statistics Reports 75-02, Births: Final Data for 2024, the figure the PCV21 vaccine seed carries) / 300,000 (Sjouke et al., as prevalence) = 12.1
incidence.note: The lepodisiran seed's method for a congenital lipid trait. The engine passes it through eligible_pct, which approximates the children who turn 12 each year
incidence.check: Book: PCV21 seed carries 3,628,934 US births in 2024 (NVSR 75-02). 3,628,934 / 300,000 = 12.096 = 12.1, on the confirmed prevalence rate. Engine check (backend/forecast.py): incidence is multiplied by eligible_pct (and the ex-US multiple), giving 10.4 a year into the 12-and-over pool; the true inflow is the cohort turning 12 (about 13 a year), a difference of 3 patients a year against a pool near 1,000.

eligible_pct.source: YOSEMITE entry (NCT07037771; Arrowhead release via search): aged 12 and over, genetic or clinical HoFH, on maximally tolerated lipid-lowering therapy, with an LDL-C floor (116 mg/dL for adolescents). Age share from the book's Census figures: 266,978,268 adults (Census Vintage 2024, the AZD0780 seed) plus the 12-to-17 cohort taken as six birth cohorts of 4,247,694 (US births 2008, CDC NCHS Births: Final Data for 2008, the lepodisiran seed), over 340,110,988 residents: (266,978,268 + 25,486,164) / 340,110,988 = 0.8599
eligible_pct.note: The label population is expected to match YOSEMITE's age floor; no LDL-C filter is applied because Evkeeza's label carries none and the uptake below is calibrated on this same pool. JUDGEMENT on the adolescent approximation: 2008 falls inside the 2006 to 2012 births of those aged 12 to 17 in mid-2024 and is a little above their average, while child mortality and net migration are ignored; the error is under one point. Case for lower: HoFH shortens life, so adults are a smaller share of HoFH patients than of the population; a separate 12-patient adolescent Phase 3 (NCT07473843, completion 2028-07) suggests the first label may be adults only (0.785); and 79% of HICC patients in high-income countries were above their LDL-C goal (Tromp et al., Lancet 2022), so a label or payer floor would trim a little. Case for higher: Evkeeza now reaches age 1, which zodasiran does not
eligible_pct.check: Book: 266,978,268 adults (AZD0780, lepodisiran, cagrilintide seeds, Census SCPRC-EST2024-18+POP) and 4,247,694 births in 2008 (lepodisiran, olpasiran seeds). (266,978,268 + 6 x 4,247,694) / 340,110,988 = 0.85991. YOSEMITE enrols aged 12 and over (book trials title 'Adolescent and Adult Subjects'; release via search 'over the age of 12'). Judgement labelled; the adult-only case (0.785) is fair given the separate adolescent Phase 3 NCT07473843.

untreated_carryover_pct.source: derived to hold the pool at its measured size, the method of the book's remternetug seed: 1,133.7 / (1,133.7 + 12.1) = 0.9894
untreated_carryover_pct.note: JUDGEMENT. The engine has no death term, so at 1.0 the untreated pool would grow by the births every year. The prevalence is a genetic frequency on the living population, which is stationary by construction. The same retention is used in the Evkeeza fit below. The effect is small either way: 12 a year against a pool of about 1,000
untreated_carryover_pct.check: 1,133.7 / (1,133.7 + 12.096) = 0.98944, the retention = pool / (pool + inflow) method the brief names and the remternetug seed uses (book: 15.87 / (15.87 + 1.95) = 0.8906). Judgement labelled.

penetration_peak_pct.unit: share of the untreated eligible pool per year
penetration_peak_pct.source: Solved from Evkeeza's own US launch (FDA approval February 2021), fitting the engine's identity (backend/forecast.py derive_new_patients and treated_stock) to its filed US net sales read at this seed's net price. Sales: $18.4mm 2021 (Regeneron FY2021 results, seen via search), $48.6mm 2022, $77.3mm 2023, $125.7mm 2024 (FY2024 10-K 0001804220-25-000011), $162.2mm 2025 (FY2025 10-K 0000872589-26-000008), $99.0mm in H1 2026 (10-Q 0000872589-26-000025: Q1 $45.7mm, Q2 $53.3mm), annualised. Net price $327,110 in 2024, scaled for 2021 to 2023 by CMS Part B spend per claim ($36,392, $36,230, $39,508 against $40,378; lookup.py demand Evkeeza), gives patient-equivalents of 62, 166, 242, 384, 496 and 605. Pool 975 aged 12 and over (1,133.7 x 0.8599), inflow 10.4 a year, retention 0.9894, discontinuation 0.0451, k fixed at 0.657. Least squares: peak 0.2972, midpoint 2.13 years from 2021, fitted 58, 145, 258, 384, 502, 598, rmse 11.65 (the researcher's 0.290 and 2.05 fit at rmse 11.79 and are not the minimum). Zodasiran: 0.5 x 0.2972 = 0.1486
penetration_peak_pct.note: JUDGEMENT: a multiple of 0.5 on Evkeeza's fitted capture. Evkeeza already holds most of this pool in the engine's units, so zodasiran's starts after a 2029 launch are mostly switches, and the engine, which sees the whole pool as open, needs the lower rate. Engine check at this seed's fields (US plus ex-US, before probability of success, loss of exclusivity and share): $13mm in 2029, $129mm in 2033, $236mm in 2037, about $279mm by 2042, US stock peaking near 627 in 2043, 64% of the pool. Units: the fit's patients are per-beneficiary equivalents, 1.51 per full-year patient; at a full-year net price of $495,200 the same fit reads peak 0.145 (midpoint 1.39, rmse 6.6 on 41 to 400 patients) and zodasiran at half gives US revenue within 7% of this path to 2041, about 22% higher by 2048. Case for higher: 4 subcutaneous injections a year against 13 IV infusions, and Arrowhead's low-price habit could win payer preference. Case for lower: Evkeeza reaches age 1 and has long-term and real-world data; the efficacy rests on a 70-patient trial not yet read out; CTX310, a one-time ANGPTL3 editor, is in Phase 1. Evkeeza's curve cannot separate peak from steepness over 5.5 years (profile: k 0.40 gives peak 0.57, midpoint 4.95, rmse 9.3; k 1.0 rmse 18.1), so the 0.297 depends on the borrowed k
penetration_peak_pct.check: Rebuilt the fit with the engine's identity from backend/forecast.py. The researcher's fitted series (59, 146, 259, 384, 500, 595) reproduces exactly at peak 0.290, midpoint 2.05, but the least-squares minimum on the same data and pool is peak 0.2972, midpoint 2.13 (rmse 11.65 vs 11.79), so half is 0.1486, not 0.145. Inputs confirmed: sales in the book's filings (2022 to H1 2026) and by search (2021 $18.4mm), CMS spend per claim from lookup.py, pool 975 settled as above. The pool is not changed (see prevalence), so the fit is not moved further. Pool sensitivity for the record: at 1:250,000 (pool 1,170) the fit reads 0.210; at 1:360,000 (812) 0.458. Researcher's k profile confirmed (k 0.40: rmse 9.3, peak 0.57; k 1.0: 18.1). Old 0.145 -> new 0.1486; engine effect about +1%.

ramp_steepness.source: the book's lipid-injectable k: Leqvio's CMS Part D beneficiaries 721 in 2022 to 2,681 in 2024 (lookup.py demand Leqvio), ln(2,681 / 721) / 2 = 0.657, carried by the olpasiran, lepodisiran, enlicitide, AZD0780 and ziltivekimab seeds (lookup.py seed Olpasiran)
ramp_steepness.note: JUDGEMENT on the analogue: an infrequently dosed siRNA lipid injectable. It is also consistent with Evkeeza's own series: profiling the fit over k, 0.40 to 0.66 all fit within 12 patients rmse, while k of 1.0 or more fits worse (18 to 23). Case for faster: a switch launch into a small, specialist-managed pool can move quickly (Vabysmo's fitted k is 1.685)
ramp_steepness.check: lookup.py demand Leqvio: Part D beneficiaries 721 (2022) and 2,681 (2024); ln(2,681/721)/2 = 0.6567. lookup.py seed Olpasiran carries ramp_steepness 0.657 from the same series. The profile claim holds: on Evkeeza's own data, k 0.40 to 0.66 fit within 12 patients rmse (9.3 to 11.7), k 1.0 fits at 18.1 and 1.2 at 21.4. Vabysmo's fitted k of 1.685 is in the book (MK-8748 seed).

ramp_midpoint_year.source: Evkeeza's least-squares midpoint at k 0.657 on the 975-patient pool, counted from 2021, its launch year (see penetration_peak_pct): 2.13 years, with peak 0.2972
ramp_midpoint_year.note: Reused from the incumbent's own launch. Leqvio's 5-year midpoint was not taken: it reflects slow uptake in mass cardiovascular prevention, not a rare-disease specialist market
ramp_midpoint_year.check: Same refit as penetration_peak_pct: the joint least-squares minimum is midpoint 2.13 with peak 0.2972 (rmse 11.65); 2.05 was paired with 0.290, which is off the minimum. Old 2.05 -> new 2.13.
